messages:
Maya (Support): FYI - Customer ACME reported repeated 504s & timeouts hitting the hosted /v1/generate endpoint starting ~10:12 UTC. Ticket: #8743. They included a reproducible curl and trace id. I'm pasting key info below — triage help needed, this looks like a queue saturation / tail-latency issue on the continuous-batching path.

Maya (Support): Symptom summary: ~2–3% request rate for that tenant returned 504 gateway_timeout with upstream 'request queue timeout' message. P95 for that route jumped from ~180ms to >4s and P99s spiked to 15–30s. Customer seeing timeouts in prod, very upset.

Maya (Support): Example error in gateway logs:

```
[2026-02-07T10:13:02Z] request_id=rid_0a1b2c upstream_status=504 upstream_error="request_queue_timeout" route=/v1/generate tenant=acme-corp
```

Maya (Support): Sample curl customer used to repro (redacted API key):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "redwood/gpt-xl", "prompt": "<very long prompt...>", "max_tokens": 1024, "stream": false}'
```

Maya (Support): Observed pattern: heavy long-sequence prompts + concurrent burst across sessions => backlog in continuous-batcher. Customer saw best-effort retries but they just hit queue early-reject sometimes.

OpsBot: Alert fired: queue_depth_high / continuous_batcher backlog on pool hosted-eu-1 (threshold 80%). Current: 93% (sustained 6m).

Devon (Eng-runtime): Thanks, grabbing traces. Does customer include request_ids? Maya, can you paste 2-3 request ids and the route (should be /v1/generate)? Also which model variant — quantized vs fp16?

Maya (Support): Provided in ticket: rid_0a1b2c, rid_0a1b2d, rid_0a1b2e. Model: redwood/gpt-xl-fp16. Workload: concurrent 40 req/s from a single tenant, average input tokens ~1.2k.

Devon (Eng-runtime): Ok. Early hypothesis: big prompts produce large KV lengths and high decoding time which reduces batching throughput; continuous batcher accumulates requests waiting for token generation capacity and hits max_queue_depth causing gateway to return early 504s. Possible contributor: current batcher target max latency is 200ms and batch growth heuristics allow large batches when inputs are long — causing a buildup tail.

Linh (Eng-SRE): I'm seeing matching metrics in prometheus for the tenant's assigned pool. Queries: `sum(rate(request_queue_depth{pool="hosted-eu-1"}[1m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))` — P99 sharp increase around 10:12 UTC. Also noticed autoscaler didn't add extra workers because utilization was under the cpu/gpu trigger — batcher backlog kept GPUs busy but scaling rules look at pod CPU which remained <70%.

Devon (Eng-runtime): That mismatch is classic — long in-GPU time but low CPU. We should adjust metrics used for autoscaling to include GPU busy / batcher queue length. Short-term mitigation: reduce `max_queue_depth` for that pool and enable earlier reject (fail-fast) for very long requests or route them to smaller model.

Maya (Support): Customer asked for repro steps and a mitigation they can apply client-side quickly. Suggested they limit concurrency and reduce max_tokens. They asked if we have an immediate server-side knob.

Linh (Eng-SRE): I can bump worker count on hosted-eu-1 by +2 for the pool; that'll help throughput. Doing now with canary so we can roll back.

deploy-bot: Started scale-up: hosted-eu-1 pool +2 workers. Rollout id=roll_1842004359 status=starting

Devon (Eng-runtime): In parallel I recommend changing batcher config for that pool to lower `batch_wait_ms` from 50 -> 25 and set `max_queue_depth` from 200 -> 120. That will reduce tail-accumulation at cost of some throughput. We should also enable per-tenant early-reject if local queue depth > 100.

Maya (Support): Is the batcher config change hot-reloadable? Can we do that without restart?

Devon (Eng-runtime): Yes, batcher tuning is hot-reloadable for hosted pools. I'll stage the change and flip it live once SRE confirms scale-up. Proposed change snippet: 

```
batcher: {
  batch_wait_ms: 25,
  max_batch_tokens: 8192,
  max_queue_depth: 120,
  early_reject_enabled: true,
  per_tenant_queue_limit: 100
}
```

Devon (Eng-runtime): Also adding a short-term fallback route so when queue depth exceeds 85% we route new tenant requests to `redwood/gpt-medium` automatically (lower cost/latency) — login pages are unaffected but generation quality downscales.

Linh (Eng-SRE): scale-up completed, verifying GPU metrics... GPUs report higher utilization now and throughput increased. Prometheus shows queue_depth dropping from 93% to ~62% within 90s.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: roll_1842004359 status=success

Maya (Support): Customer reports reduced errors after ~3 minutes, but still hitting intermittent 504s under sustained load. They want root cause and prevention.

Devon (Eng-runtime): Next steps for root cause: 1) collect detailed batcher traces around the three request_ids (rid_0a1b2c/d/e) to inspect batching decisions 2) examine per-request kv_size and decode steps to see if a few heavy requests block many small ones 3) instrument autoscaler to consider `gpu_busy_seconds` and `batcher_queue_length` metrics.

Maya (Support): I pulled a trace for rid_0a1b2c: shows it sat in batch_queue for 3.8s before being accepted into a batch, then decode time ~2.1s. Customer's client-side timeout default was 4s, so they got 504 while request still in queue.

Devon (Eng-runtime): That matches backlog-caused tail-latency. We should: A) implement per-tenant shaping (max concurrent inflight) B) improve early-reject policy to return a 429 rather than 504 when queue is overloaded so clients can backoff properly C) expose queue_depth metrics per-tenant to customers so they can adapt.

Carlos (Customer Success): I'll draft a proactive message to ACME explaining we throttled to protect platform, we scaled the pool, and next steps to avoid recurrence (reduce concurrency, shorter inputs). Offer 10% credit for the window and a follow-up review with Eng.

Linh (Eng-SRE): Filed infra follow-ups: INFRA-2193 (autoscaler metric add), INFRA-2194 (per-tenant queue metrics), RUNTIME-3421 (early-reject 429). Assigning owners.

Devon (Eng-runtime): For immediate monitoring: run these PromQL checks: 

```
max_over_time(request_queue_depth{pool="hosted-eu-1"}[10m]) > 150
sum(rate(decode_time_seconds_sum{pool="hosted-eu-1"}[1m])) by (model)
```

Devon (Eng-runtime): Also putting a small patch to batcher to prefer admitting smaller inputs first (age-adjusted priority) — that should reduce tail for mixed workloads. I'll open PR and tag SRE for review.

Maya (Support): Customer asked how to reproduce for our internal tests. Repro steps I used locally:

1) spawn 40 concurrent curl sessions using the long prompt payload above
2) set client timeout to 3s to observe failures
3) monitor `request_queue_depth` and `batcher_backlog` in Grafana for hosted-eu-1

Maya (Support): Quick repro script (basic):

```
for i in {1..40}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @long_payload.json &
done
wait
```

Linh (Eng-SRE): Copying runbook pointer: runbooks/queue-backpressure.md — follow sections: 'scale pool', 'apply batcher hotfix', 'notify customer'.

Devon (Eng-runtime): PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1845 — patch adds small-input priority + config toggles. Marking high priority.

Maya (Support): ACME confirmed decreased error rate after scale + config change. They want a postmortem/summary and assurance we won't flip to early 429s without warning.

Carlos (Customer Success): I'll coordinate the PM/CS engagement and schedule a 1:1 with their infra lead. Also propose a short post-incident summary to be shared.

Devon (Eng-runtime): Longer-term work items: - tune autoscaler triggers to include GPU busy and batcher metrics - add tenant-level rate limiting knobs in Console - improve batching heuristics for mixed-length workloads - expose a 'probable-queue-delay' header so SDKs can auto-backoff.

Linh (Eng-SRE): Closing live incident: service degraded -> mitigated. Follow-ups filed INFRA-2193, INFRA-2194, RUNTIME-3421, RUNTIME-3422 (batcher priority).

Maya (Support): Thanks all. I'll update the ticket with mitigation timeline, customer credits, and link to PRs/runbooks. Marking this thread resolved for now, please ping if anything changes. :white_check_mark:

Devon (Eng-runtime): Adding note — please re-open if any other tenant shows similar pattern. I'll keep the PR and batcher flags under observation for the next 48h. :eyes:
